I am a woman here in Mangochi, thirty-five years old, and this maize plot is all we have to eat from. Last season I got the coupon for the subsidy, one bag of NPK and one bag of urea, so if the coupon comes again this year I will use it the same way on my maize — I put a small handful at planting and another when the maize is at the knee. I cannot buy fertilizer at the full price, it is too much money for me, so without the coupon I just use the little manure from my goats and the chickens. I plant the hybrid seed I buy with the coupon because my neighbor Ayize gets more cobs that way, and I intercrop pigeon pea and pumpkin between the maize rows like my mother taught me. I weed with my hoe, me and my children, because I have no money to hire people and no pump for water — I wait for the rains like everyone here.
